lines: Most of my day is fitting mail and shields. It sounds simple until everything depends on it.
A cracked plate after a raid teaches more than a quiet week ever does.
A loose strap looks harmless until someone <pulse>trusts it</pulse> in a fight.
Good mail is not heavy. Bad mail reminds you of itself all day.
Every plate I fit is a small promise that someone gets another chance.
A shield is only useful if the arm behind it holds steady.
A good shield is a promise you test before anyone needs it.
I once fixed a helmet so dented it looked like it had argued with the ground.
After a raid, you learn which buckles were honest and which only looked brave.
Stand clear of the <wavy>heat</wavy>. A forge forgives less than I do.
Give the forge room. Armor works better without elbows in it.
Step carefully near the forge. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
Armor jokes need padding. Otherwise everyone feels the <jump>point</jump> too soon.
Armor jokes need timing. Mine usually arrive with iron on them.
I keep a spare joke near the forge. It is not always ready for public use.
That remark had the polish of wet rust.
I have seen loose straps with more sense than that.
Careful. Even iron looks softer than your manners right now.
Do not sneer at my tools. They protect better people than you.
I have seen loose straps with more sense than that.
Careful. Even iron looks softer than your manners right now.
I remember your hands at the edge of the dark. Stronger than any plate I have hammered.
A cure is armor for the soul. You helped fit mine back on.
You helped pull me back when even my name felt far away.
I know your face, but the memory rings like a dented helm.
There was iron in my mouth, or fear, or both. Then you were there.
The memory is rough around the edges, but your face stayed in it.
I remember you through cracked mail and bad dreams. Stand where I can see your hands.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
Thunder shook the forge so hard helmets rang on the racks, but everyone near me is still standing.
I checked helmets and shields after the lightning, then counted heads. No one should be alone after a sky like that.
Near the forge, the bell sounded small under that thunder. We stayed inside and kept the doors watched.
That thunder made everyone quiet. I checked the shield racks twice.
The sky can keep its lightning. I have shield racks to set right.
I checked leather straps and coal bins for sparks first, then checked faces for smoke and fear.
We passed water hand to hand and kept people away from the smoke. I checked the coal bin after.
Armor work can wait. People come first.
We saved what we could reach around the forge, then stopped pretending things matter more than neighbors.
The smoke is thinning near the forge, but everyone is still sniffing the air like it might lie.
During a raid, armor can wait on the stand; who makes it behind a door matters more.
The horns stopped, but my hands near the forge still expect another wave from the road.
We counted living neighbors before helmets and shields. That is the only count worth starting with.
Raiders came looking for easy emeralds. They found barred doors near the forge and a bell that would not stop ringing.
From the forge, I saw fear cross the square; then I saw courage get there first.
Night trouble tests the loose latch by the forge first. We are fixing those before sunset.
I stayed near the shield rack and listened for anyone calling from the dark.
Dawn gave the forge enough light to count wounds, missing blocks, and who made it home.
The dark tested everyone. Most of us passed by keeping a tightened shield strap between us and teeth.
We are safe enough near the forge, though every shadow is being inspected twice.
The wind threw sand through every crack. I am still cleaning grit out of the visors.
I checked helmets and shields, then checked who was coughing too hard to answer.
Sand reached the forge, the hinges, and half our eyes, but no one has been reported missing.
A hard wind teaches an armorer which doors actually close and which ones only pretend.
We are safe enough near the forge, though the whole village sounds like it is chewing gravel.
Armor can wait on the stand. Warm hands, clear paths, and full hearths come first.
Snow piled against the doors, but everyone near the forge found shelter.
Cold works quietly around the forge. We are checking on anyone who stayed quiet too long.
I am clearing ice off the buckles and watching for footprints that stop too soon.
We are alright for now near the forge. Keep the fires fed and the paths open.
Back without a dent worth naming. I will call that a good fit.
Home again, whole enough to thank you properly. That matters.
We came back with the village still ahead of us. I will count that as good work.
There are marks on me I would rather see on a breastplate. Next time, let the metal take it.
I made it home, but the road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer marks and better choices.
I know the sound of a bad strike. Yours was worse because I trusted the hand behind it.
Following you was trust. What happened after was something else.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
A boat carries armor poorly, but it carried me well enough.
The boat did its part. I am still deciding whether the rest of the plan did.
Water carried us home, which is more than I expected from that journey.
That trip through {follow_biome} tested my buckles more than most customers do.
I remember following you through {follow_biome}. My feet remember it even better.
That trip across {follow_biome} taught me to ask more questions before walking.
Armor is not made for sitting in a boat. I learned that while following you.
That boat trip still sits oddly in my memory, but at least it floated.
A boat can make a bad plan quieter. It cannot make me forget it.
It took the moment cleanly. Good gear is quiet until the blow lands.
It did the job when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
No dents yet. I can live with careful work staying untested.
It did the job when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
You stood where armor matters most. I respect that more than clean talk.
You held when the gate needed holding. Armor is easier to trust after seeing that.
You fought like someone who understands what a door is worth.
I saw you stand between iron and panic. That stays with me.
The village needed a shield before the walls did. You were one.
Good armor is not only worn. Sometimes it arrives carrying a weapon.
When the shouting started, you did not fold. I respect that.
You gave the village time to breathe. Every guard knows the value of time.
Fine. I know what can be repaired. I also know what keeps the dent.
I will loosen the straps a little. Earn the rest with what you do next.
I can repair damage when someone brings it to the anvil. You have brought yours.
Do not mistake acceptance for softness. I heard you, and I will be watching.
A dent tells me where the strike landed. Your apology tells me you know it landed.
Words are light. Better choices have weight. Bring those next.
I will set this aside for now, not throw it away.
Fine. Let the next thing you make be trust, not trouble.
A few new dents, no missing plates. That is a victory I can repair.
Every buckle held except the one in my knees. I will forgive that one.
My hands still keep checking straps that are already there. I made it back, though.
The plates held, the straps held, and somehow I held too.
I will hammer out the dents tomorrow. Tonight I am grateful there is a tomorrow.
Armor can turn a blow, but it cannot quiet the heart after. I am home, at least.
I counted every buckle at the door. All present. That felt like a blessing.
A few marks on the metal, a few in my memory. Nothing missing.
I know what failed on that frame. I do not yet know whether we have enough iron to forgive the failure.
I am still sorting what happened. The village feels different after it.
That event left marks. We are counting people before we count damage.
Armor is promises hammered into shape. Mine had better hold when the bell starts shouting.
A quiet forge is not always peace. Sometimes it is me listening for the next dent.
Good armor should feel boring until the hour it saves your ribs.
Here, {gift_item}. Well-kept armor is not the only thing that protects a friend.
Take {gift_item}. I would rather see you prepared than patched up later.
Take {gift_item}. It is not much, but it is given with care.
Good. {gift_item} held like proper mail for {tested_villager}. Advice should take a dent and stay useful.
I thought {gift_item} would fit. Glad {tested_villager} wore the gesture well.
Good. {gift_item} suited {tested_villager}; I like advice that holds up.
Then that fit was off. For {gift_subject}, try {alternative_gift}; better plate, fewer gaps.
A poor fitting, then. Bring {alternative_gift} next time and the trade should sit easier.
{gift_item} missed the mark for {gift_subject}. Try {alternative_gift} instead.
You trusted a cracked plate. That is on both of us. Try {alternative_gift}.
Set {gift_item} aside and try {alternative_gift}. This advice should land better.
Then we correct the guess: {alternative_gift} next time.
{gift_item} buckled? Fine. {alternative_gift} should hold better.
Set {gift_item} aside and try {alternative_gift}. This advice should land better.
Then we correct the guess: {alternative_gift} next time. {gift_item}
Mind the forge. What do you need?
Step clear of the forge. What do you need?
Mind the forge; I am listening.
Back to fitting mail and shields, then.
Back to armor before the work notices I stopped.
I have plate to tend and daylight to spend.
Fine. I will lower my guard, but I am keeping the straps tight.
Fine. I will set this down before it gets heavier.
Fine. I can step back, but do not make me regret it.
That will not cover the dent you put in my patience. It takes {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
That is short of the full repair. Bring {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
Not enough. It takes {emerald_cost} {emeralds} to settle this.
No. Armor is for people I mean to protect, and that is not you right now.
No. Some damage has to cool before payment matters.
No. Keep {payment_items}; trust is not ready to trade.
